audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Skill to level 6 and Rumble to both item rows, while the whys say level 6 is where you 'snip a kill his shield and sustain can't save', first item is 'a wash', and two items is 'you're the stickier teamfight titan'. The already-written mirror at audits/top/rumble__chogath.json flagged this same contradiction in its own notes and did not fix it. diff also reads TRICKY 7.5/10 against the mirror's EVEN 6/10 on a 49.42% win rate.
audit.why: Rumble's claim on the lane is levels 2-3 while Flamespitter out-DPSes a short-ranged Cho'Gath. Feast at 6 is true damage his resistances cannot answer, and at two items Cho'Gath is a frontline Rumble has no way to kill.
audit.corrected: Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Cho'Gath / Skill / Cho'Gath — the packet chart — as one atomic group across win[0..6] and phases[0..6].side+rating, plus diff EVEN and diffRating 6/10 to align with the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase text named Heartsteel as the fight-forcing spike and 'levels 2-3 (full pattern)' as Cho'Gath's window, which is Rumble's window.
audit.why: The spikes are Danger Zone rotations at 2-3 for him, Liandry's at first item for him, and level 6 plus two items for you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three things. Missing: Junkyard Titan's Overheat — at 100 heat Rumble 'start[s] Overheating ... making him unable to cast spells for a few seconds'. That is a self-inflicted silence and it is the single best commit window in the lane, and it appears nowhere in either layer. Wrong: the entire page is built around baiting Scrap Shield, which is a flat 6 seconds — far too short to play around. Wrong: spikes[2].text credits Vorpal Spikes with 'percent max-HP autos'; Riot's description gives it damage and a slow, with no percent-health component anywhere.
audit.why: Telling the player to wait out a 6s shield instead of counting a heat bar is the difference between never finding a window and getting a free one every rotation. And a fabricated percent-health mechanic on your own E will make the player misjudge how fast they actually grind him down.
audit.corrected: Overheat written into tradeGood, report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns and whys[3]; Scrap Shield demoted with its real 6s cooldown; the Vorpal Spikes percent-health claim removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Build MR' is the headline Do, with no note that Electro Harpoon reduces magic resist.
audit.why: MR is still the right buy — his whole kit is magic — but the harpoon shreds it, and the mirror already flagged that 'Build MR for his R' is wrong because Feast is true damage. So MR answers Flamespitter and the harpoon, and health has to come with it.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d re-pointed at Flamespitter and the harpoon, with the MR shred named.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns was placeholder text and named Scrap Shield as matchup-defining.
audit.why: Flamespitter at 10s rank 1 is the damage clock, Scrap Shield's 6s is not worth tracking, Electro Harpoon recharges on a 0.5s timer with two charges, and The Equalizer is 130s at rank 1. The heat bar is the real clock.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around Flamespitter, the 6s shield and the Overheat window.

notes: MIRROR: audits/top/rumble__chogath.json is already written and made no chart edits, but its own notes say phases[4], phases[5] and phases[6] contradict the level chart and that the full layer wrongly awards Rumble the 2+ items row. I have corrected that on this side to match the packet and the prose, so tools/mirror-fix.js must resolve toward this version. I also set diff/diffRating to EVEN 6/10, which now matches the Rumble page exactly rather than conflicting with it. Reused the mirror's findings rather than re-deriving: Rupture is a knockup not a grounding effect despite the derived flag, Cho'Gath's sustain is Carnivore off unit kills rather than anything on Vorpal Spikes, and 'build MR' must be pointed at Flamespitter rather than at Feast. NOT ASSERTED: whether Feral Scream can interrupt The Equalizer mid-cast. The existing late text claims a Q knockup or the silence can interrupt it; Riot's description does not call The Equalizer a channel and needsResearch.animationCancels is null for both champions, so I left that claim exactly as I found it and did not repeat or strengthen it in any field I wrote. Also not asserted: whether Overheat's spell lockout is affected by anything Cho'Gath can do, or whether Electro Harpoon's MR shred stacks between its two charges. Content 'wants.foe[2]' also implied Rumble seeks Overheat deliberately; Riot's text makes Overheat a penalty on top of an attack-speed bonus, so I re-pointed it at Danger Zone, which is the state he actually wants.
